Date: 2026-12-21 | Time: 15:00 EST | Duration: 48m
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Ava Cruz (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Laura Kim (Fairview CISO), Daniel Ortiz (Fairview Head of Cloud), Priya Shah (Fairview Compliance), Marcus Lee (Platform)
Links shared: redwood.com/soc2 (placeholder), redwood.com/hipaa-pack (placeholder), drive.fairview/ppi-flows (customer link, not captured)
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, with Ava and Samir on the call. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Laura: Hi Jordan, thanks, yea doing well. We carved out this slot to talk specifically about data residency and compliance for a potential rollout next Q1.
[00:15] Jordan: Great, objective for today is to understand your constraints (GDPR, HIPAA, logging), current architecture and decision criteria for hosted vs dedicated vs private. We'll also capture next steps.
[00:28] Daniel: Quick note, our main driver is EU data residency for EU customers and a couple of lines of business that handle health-related data—so HIPAA applies. Also bank regs, so audit logs and limited retention are big.
[00:40] Ava: Understood. Could you walk through current stack and where data lives today?
[00:45] Marcus: Sure. We run most services in AWS, accounts split by region. Customer data for EU is in eu-west-1. We have a central logging account that pulls logs, but for some systems we have stricter retention—like 90 days for certain PII.
[01:02] Priya: And from compliance side we need to ensure that any inference requests that touch EU customer PII do not leave EU, and that logs containing request payloads are either disabled or scrubbed.
[01:14] Samir: Right—so two asks: residency of inference (model hosting in EU), and control over logs/payloads. On the latter, Redwood hosted defaults to ephemeral logs but we do capture traces for debugging; do you require zero retention or redact-at-source?
[01:28] Priya: Preferably redact-at-source, and for certain workflows, zero persistent logs. Also need KMS-backed encryption keys we control.
[01:36] Jordan: For Key Management we support customer-managed keys (KMS) in Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports provider KMS with BYOK options on enterprise plans—though for HIPAA/FSI customers we usually recommend Dedicated or Private so keys don't leave the customer tenancy.
[01:52] Laura: Can you explain the difference in practice? Like, what does Dedicated buy us vs Private?
[01:57] Ava: Sure. Hosted means our multi-tenant managed control plane. Dedicated is reserved capacity with isolation at the serving layer—compute pools dedicated to you, but control plane still managed by Redwood. Private means control plane and optionally data plane in your VPC or on-prem; you manage network and optionally keys.
[02:16] Marcus: So for Private we'd host the control plane in our VPC?
[02:19] Ava: Exactly. Private gives you a customer-managed control plane, optional on-prem packages, and KMS/HSM integrations. That helps with auditability and reduce logs leaving your boundary.
[02:27] Daniel: What about SOC 2 and HIPAA attestations on Hosted? We can't move forward without docs.
[02:33] Jordan: We have SOC 2 Type II and a HIPAA compliance pack we can share. I'll drop the links after the call. For the hosted plan there are contractual terms covering PHI handling.
[02:44] Priya: Regarding logging, you said hosted captures traces. Can those be disabled?
[02:49] Samir: There's a couple knobs. You can disable request logging, enable prefix caching only, and we can route telemetry to your logging sink in Dedicated/Private. Hosted by default keeps short-term traces for debugging but we can offer redaction and suppression via enterprise agreement.
[03:03] Laura: One technical concern—how do you ensure inference doesn't route to non-EU hardware? We need guarantee that EU requests stay within EU.
[03:11] Ava: We support region pinning and smart routing policies. For Dedicated you can provision capacity in eu-west-1 and we route requests there. For Hosted, we have region-specific endpoints; EU traffic can be pinned to EU model instances. For highest assurance Private is best because you completely control where instances run.
[03:29] Marcus: Are there fallbacks? If eu capacity is saturated will requests spill to us-east?
[03:34] Jordan: Policies can be set to fail closed—that is, don't route outside EU; or fail open to a compatible model in another region if you prefer availability. We'll capture your preference.
[03:44] Daniel: On encryption—at rest and in transit—what's the story? We need TLS in transit and AES-256 at rest with keys in our AWS KMS.
[03:54] Samir: We encrypt in transit via TLS and at rest with AES-256. Dedicated and Private support customer-managed KMS keys; Private can integrate with HSM for stronger guarantees. Hosted can do BYOK under EKM arrangements for enterprise.
[04:10] Priya: For HIPAA we also need Business Associate Agreement (BAA). Do you sign BAAs?
[04:15] Jordan: Yes, Redwood executes BAAs with customers that require them. I'll include our legal contact and the BAA template in the pack.
[04:24] Laura: Logging retention—some of our teams need logs retained for a year, others we want zero retention. Can that be per-route?
[04:32] Ava: Yes, Redwood supports per-route logging policies; you can set retention windows and choose whether request payloads are included. On Dedicated/Private you get more granular control. Hosted supports route-level settings but some backend debugging artifacts may persist short-term unless suppressed via agreement.
[04:48] Marcus: How about redaction? For instance, PII like SSNs in prompts—can we configure automatic redaction or scrub before logs are stored?
[04:57] Samir: We provide server-side redaction rules and recommend client-side scrubbing prior to sending. We also have a feature for pre-request transformers to strip or tokenise sensitive fields before they reach the model. Some of that is available in Dedicated/Private first.
[05:13] Daniel: Performance-wise, we run gen models for chat; latency SLOs are critical. If we go Private and run on-prem GPUs, do you support model variants and quantization?
[05:22] Ava: Yes, our runtime supports quantized execution and model variants. On Private you can pin specific kernels and we provide a runtime image that supports our KV cache and batching logic. We typically work with your infra team to match hardware and provide recommended configs.
[05:37] Laura: Regulatory question—do you provide audit logs with immutable entries and export capabilities for auditors?
[05:43] Jordan: Yes. Audit logs and admin actions are exported to sinks. In Private you can store logs in your own S3 / logging solution; for Hosted we can push exports to your project but may need arrangement for long term retention.
[05:57] Priya: One more, can we restrict what engineers can see in transcripts? We need RBAC so only certain people can view full request/response.
[06:05] Samir: RBAC is supported; role-level masking for request payloads and a separate permission for viewing raw outputs. We can sync to your SSO (SAML/Okta) and enforce least privilege.
[06:18] Marcus: Sounds promising. Any suggested architecture for hybrid: some workloads in Hosted, sensitive workflows in Private?
[06:26] Ava: That's common. Many customers use Hosted for low-sensitivity traffic and dedicated/private for EU/HIPAA/FSI flows. Smart routing, canary policies, and model fallbacks keep behavior consistent. We'll draft a reference architecture.
[06:40] Laura: Pricing concerns—if we have reserved capacity for Dedicated in EU region, is that monthly commit?
[06:46] Jordan: Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits; we can provide capacity planning guidance. Private has different licensing plus infra costs. We'll include a pricing sketch in the follow-up.
[06:57] Daniel: On legal—data residency proofs for auditors—do you provide attestation statements showing models hosted in region X during date ranges?
[07:05] Samir: We can provide logs and deployment records showing host region and instance IDs for auditing. For Private you can produce your own provenance since you control infra.
[07:15] Priya: One quirky thing—our legal team is strict about third-party logs, they want to know if Redwood's devs ever access customer content for debugging.
[07:24] Jordan: With Dedicated/Private, dev access is highly restricted; access is logged and requires approvals. Hosted support allows redaction and a support workflow where content is only accessed with consent. We'll document the support access process.
[07:40] Laura: Great. Can you also show how retention settings look in the console? A UI screenshot or quick demo would help.
[07:47] Ava: Yep, we'll schedule a short console demo. I'll include examples of per-route retention, redaction rules, and KMS settings.
[07:56] Jordan: Recap of next steps—I'll send SOC2/HIPAA pack and BAA template; Ava will schedule architecture deep-dive and demo; Daniel to send PII dataflows. Anything else?
[08:07] Daniel: That's it from us. Quick question—do you have customers in banking with similar needs?
[08:12] Jordan: Yes, we have references in financial services and a few customers using Private for EU/HIPAA workloads. I'll include anonymised references.
[08:22] Priya: Timeline—we're aiming for a pilot in late Q1, so need documentation and an initial architecture before end of this year.
[08:30] Jordan: We'll prioritize.
[08:33] [crosstalk, wrap-up]
[08:40] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with materials and actions.
[08:44] Laura: Thanks all.
[08:46] [call ends]

Notes on transcript quality: a few words mis-transcribed (e.g., K V C cache -> KV cache, V P C -> VPC), speaker overlap occasionally, filler words present.
